title: Ad Tracking & Targeted Advertising Security Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to stop ad tracking and prevent targeted advertising. Block behavioral ads and protect your privacy from advertiser surveillance.
intro: Advertisers track your every move online to build detailed profiles for targeted ads. This comprehensive checklist helps you reclaim your privacy by blocking ad tracking, preventing behavioral profiling, and stopping creepy retargeted ads from following you across the web.

items.task: Enable strict tracking protection in your browser
items.why: Blocks most tracking scripts and cross-site cookies used by advertisers to follow you across websites.
items.howTo: In Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Third-party cookies > Block third-party cookies. In Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > Enhanced Tracking Protection > Strict.

items.task: Block all third-party cookies
items.why: Third-party cookies are the primary method advertisers use to track you across different websites and build behavioral profiles.
items.howTo: Go to browser settings, find Privacy/Security section, locate cookies settings, and select 'Block third-party cookies' or 'Block all cookies from sites you haven't visited'.

items.task: Turn off ad personalization in browser settings
items.why: Prevents your browser from sharing browsing data with advertisers for personalized ad targeting.
items.howTo: Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Ad privacy > Ad topics, Site-suggested ads, Ad measurement - turn all off. Edge: Settings > Privacy > General > toggle off ad personalization.

items.task: Clear all browsing data and cookies regularly
items.why: Removes existing tracking data that advertisers have already collected about your browsing habits.
items.howTo: Press Ctrl+Shift+Delete (Cmd+Shift+Delete on Mac), select 'All time', check cookies, browsing history, cached images, and click Clear data. Set up automatic clearing if available.

items.task: Use private/incognito browsing mode regularly
items.why: Prevents tracking cookies from being stored and limits cross-site tracking during your browsing session.
items.howTo: Use Ctrl+Shift+N for Chrome incognito or Ctrl+Shift+P for Firefox private browsing. Consider a privacy-focused browser for enhanced privacy protection with built-in ad blocking.

items.task: Block location access for advertising purposes
items.why: Prevents location-based targeted advertising and stops advertisers from tracking your physical movements.
items.howTo: Browser settings > Privacy > Location > Block all sites from accessing location, or prompt for each request. Also disable location history in your Google/Microsoft account.

items.task: Install a comprehensive ad blocker extension
items.why: Blocks display ads, tracking scripts, and behavioral advertising networks from loading on websites you visit.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin from your browser's extension store. Enable all filter lists including tracking protection, malware domains, and privacy filters for maximum protection.

items.task: Switch to a privacy-focused browser
items.why: Privacy browsers have built-in tracking protection and don't collect data for advertising purposes like mainstream browsers.
items.howTo: Download privacy-focused browsers like Firefox with strict settings, or Brave. These block trackers by default and don't send data to advertising companies.

items.task: Enable comprehensive tracking protection filter lists
items.why: Blocks known advertising and tracking domains from loading, preventing behavioral profiling and cross-site tracking.
items.howTo: In uBlock Origin: Dashboard > Filter lists > Enable Privacy, Malware Domains, Annoyances. Also add EasyPrivacy and Fanboy's Enhanced Tracking List for comprehensive protection.

items.task: Use a script blocker for advanced protection
items.why: Prevents tracking scripts and advertising JavaScript from running, stopping sophisticated fingerprinting and behavioral tracking.
items.howTo: Install NoScript (Firefox) or ScriptSafe (Chrome). Start with default-deny settings and only allow scripts from trusted sites you frequently use.

items.task: Switch to a privacy-focused search engine
items.why: Mainstream search engines track your queries to build advertising profiles. Privacy search engines don't track or profile users.
items.howTo: Change default search engine to DuckDuckGo, Startpage, or Searx. In browser settings > Search engine > Manage search engines, set privacy option as default.

items.task: Disable Google ad personalization completely
items.why: Google tracks across millions of websites and apps to build detailed profiles for targeted advertising.
items.howTo: Go to myaccount.google.com/data-and-privacy > Ad settings. Turn off 'Ad Personalization'. Also visit adssettings.google.com and opt out of all categories and interests.

items.task: Turn off Facebook ad targeting and data collection
items.why: Facebook tracks users across the web through pixels and plugins to target ads based on off-platform activity.
items.howTo: Facebook Settings > Privacy > Ad Preferences > Ad settings. Turn off ads based on data from partners, ads based on your activity, and ads with social information. Clear all interests.

items.task: Opt out of Microsoft advertising personalization
items.why: Microsoft collects data across Windows, Bing, and partner sites for targeted advertising in their network.
items.howTo: Go to account.microsoft.com/privacy/ad-settings and turn off 'Personalized ads in this browser' and 'Personalized ads wherever I use my Microsoft account'.

items.task: Disable Amazon advertising personalization
items.why: Amazon uses purchase history and browsing data to target ads across their platform and partner sites.
items.howTo: Amazon account > Privacy Preferences > Advertising Preferences > turn off 'Personalized ads' and 'Ads from Amazon's ad server based on interest categories'.

items.task: Use industry-wide advertising opt-out tools
items.why: Opts you out of hundreds of advertising networks and data brokers at once that participate in self-regulation programs.
items.howTo: Visit optout.networkadvertising.org and optout.aboutads.info. Click 'Opt out of all' to disable targeting from participating advertising networks and data collection companies.

items.task: Disable mobile advertising identifiers
items.why: Mobile advertising IDs allow apps to track you across different applications and build behavioral profiles for targeted ads.
items.howTo: iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Apple Advertising > turn off Personalized Ads. Android: Settings > Privacy > Ads > Delete advertising ID or Opt out of Ads Personalization.

items.task: Use a VPN to prevent IP-based tracking
items.why: Masks your IP address and location, preventing advertisers from building location profiles and tracking across sessions.
items.howTo: Subscribe to a no-logs VPN service like NordVPN, ExpressVPN, or Mullvad. Connect before browsing to mask your real IP address from advertising networks.

items.task: Set up DNS-level ad and tracker blocking
items.why: Blocks tracking and advertising domains at the network level, preventing connections to known advertising and analytics servers.
items.howTo: Change DNS settings to privacy-focused providers: Quad9 (9.9.9.9), AdGuard DNS (94.140.14.14), or NextDNS with custom blocklists enabled.

items.task: Block email tracking pixels and links
items.why: Email tracking pixels report when you open emails and track clicks, feeding data to advertising profiles.
items.howTo: Enable 'Load remote content' blocking in your email client. Use email aliases from services like SimpleLogin or AnonAddy for signups to prevent cross-platform tracking.

items.task: Block social media tracking widgets
items.why: Social media buttons and widgets on websites track you even if you don't click them, building profiles of your browsing habits.
items.howTo: In uBlock Origin, enable 'Block social media icons clicking which leads to privacy breach'. Use container extensions to isolate social media sites from other browsing.

items.task: Enable anti-fingerprinting measures
items.why: Prevents websites from creating unique fingerprints of your device and browser for tracking purposes when cookies are blocked.
items.howTo: Firefox: about:config > privacy.resistFingerprinting = true. Use browsers like a privacy-focused browser or Tor Browser that have built-in fingerprinting protection.

pro_tips: Use separate browsers for different activities - one for work, one for personal browsing, and one for shopping to prevent cross-contamination of tracking data.
Regularly audit your Google Takeout data and Facebook 'Your Information' to see what advertising data companies have collected about you.
Create email aliases for different services to prevent companies from building unified profiles by matching email addresses across platforms.
Consider using a privacy-focused browser as your daily driver - it comes with built-in ad blocking and tracking protection enabled by default.
Set calendar reminders every 3 months to review and clear your advertising preferences across major platforms as they often reset or add new tracking methods.
